# Single-crystal structure search and assessment

!!! note "Shared Rust/Python model"
    These equations define the native implementation used by both APIs.
    Python users reach it through `phasesmith.single_crystal.solution`, `phasesmith.single_crystal.workflow`. The Rust owner names below
    identify implementation boundaries; they do not imply a separate Python model.


Native phasing/fitting belongs to `phasesmith-single-crystal::solution`; symmetry assessment,
model catalogues and adaptive effort belong to
`phasesmith-workflows::single_crystal`. This is non-resonant X-ray structure
search with declared cell/element or full-cell composition priors. A bounded
candidate and internal coordinate/ADP polish do not constitute a general
structure-refinement workflow.

## Observations, symmetry and amplitudes

Inputs retain signed I(hkl) and strictly positive sigma(I). Supplied exact
symmetry, supplied intensity-symmetry priors and unknown-group assessment are
distinct modes. Only genuinely measured rows provide symmetry/absence evidence;
a masked pixel, unmeasured crossing or failed integration is not I=0.

For a declared equivalence family, with `w_i=1/sigma_i^2`:

```text
I_mean = sum(w_i I_i) / sum(w_i)
sigma_mean = 1/sqrt(sum(w_i))
Fo = sqrt(max(I_mean,0)).
```

The last line is a derived phasing approximation with weak-intensity bias;
the original signed data are not overwritten. Non-resonant Friedel symmetry
permits opposite-index merging. Known systematic absences are excluded/counted
under supplied symmetry, while an unknown-group workflow keeps measured
contradictions for common-data assessment.

Exact absence reasoning uses the stabilizer operations for which R.T h=h and
their phases `exp(2*pi*i*h·t)`, with rational translations and exact operation
sets. Pure centring translations are distinguished from unknown screw/glide
translations. Metric compatibility permits a group hypothesis; it never proves
the measured intensity symmetry or uniqueness of a setting.

## Atomic amplitudes and dual-space maps

With fractional `x_j` and Cartesian q in Å^-1:

```text
F(h) = sum_j f_j(s) exp(-2*pi^2 q.T U_j q) exp(2*pi*i*h·x_j)
s = |q|/2
rho = FFT(F).real / N; F = N IFFT(rho), N=Nx*Ny*Nz.
```

The FFT signs and normalization follow the stated `NumPy` convention and are
independently checked. Map values are arbitrary normalized units, not calibrated
electrons/Å^3. Measured indices must not alias a grid/Nyquist boundary. The
measured-resolution sphere includes its boundary within the declared relative
rounding tolerance; coefficients outside it are zero.

For charge flipping, initial phases obey Hermitian symmetry; F(000) starts at
zero and is subsequently free. With fixed
`delta=delta_sigma*std(rho_initial)`, samples below delta change sign, while
samples at or above it remain unchanged. Measured magnitudes are reimposed after
transformation; unmeasured interior coefficients are free and known absences
remain zero. Optional weak-reflection and Patterson/atomic dual-space strategies
have distinct named controls. They are not interchangeable defaults.

Native peaks use periodic neighbours, deterministic ties and bounded count/label
search. A full-cell count is an explicit prior in known-composition mode, not
information inferred from a low R1. Element-type-only mode uses input-derived
resource/volume limits; no reference atom count enters its admission.

## Fitting, model comparison and acceptance

Candidate structure factors and analytical coordinate/displacement partials are
evaluated in the same reflection/image pass. A site tensor transforms as
`U_image=Q U_site Q.T`; recovery pulls equivalent tensors back before averaging.
Positive-definite parameterization and declared eigenvalue bounds apply.
Bounds, rank and true termination remain part of the result, including the
documented ADP-bound stagnation limitation.

Amplitude R1 is `sum(abs(Fo-a*abs(Fc)))/sum(Fo)` on the declared rows and scale a.
The fitting objective uses its stated normalization/weights. Unknown-group
common-data comparison uses the actual free coordinate/tensor parameters plus
scale and the native score:

```text
score = n*log(max(normalized_amplitude_SSE,1e-300)) + p*log(n).
```

Here n is the common measured-family count and p the candidate's actual parameter
count including scale. A lower own-group R1 cannot justify excluding measured
forbidden rows or replacing a better retained model with an unaccepted fallback.
Atomic-frame/origin consistency, measured symmetry contradictions, family/parameter
admission, higher-Laue/inversion evidence and close alternative groups are checked
separately. Numerical acceptance is not reference grading or proof of uniqueness.

For an intensity family with at least two Friedel-independent measurements,
the current evidence model reports chi-square about its mean with variance
`sigma^2+(0.25*abs(I))^2` and `members-1` degrees of freedom. The documented
constraint counts/thresholds are an engineering policy, not universal significance
levels; all settings and insufficient evidence remain explicit.

## Bounded effort and reproducibility

Fast/auto/thorough policies specify phase resolution, starts/cycles, model budgets
and acceptance gates. Auto may escalate only with the original remaining deadline;
explicit cancellation/total timeout do not start another pass. A deferred
numerically equivalent group remains ambiguous and unaccepted. Both actual pass
records and rejected alternatives survive. Process startup, worker count and
output are included when comparing full runtimes; kernel gains are not promoted
to whole-workflow speedups without measurements.

Publications include Oszlanyi and Suto (2004), DOI 10.1107/S0108767303027569;
their 2008 tutorial, DOI 10.1107/S0108767307046028; and Sheldrick (2015),
DOI 10.1107/S2053273314026370. The independent implementation and frozen comparison
protocols distinguish published methods from `PhaseSmith` choices. SHELXT/GSAS-II
remain external comparators, never runtime dependencies or source implementations.
The exposed 65-case and 14-case results are regression evidence; future
generalization claims require new untouched cases.
